core_obligations: Write $[Y]_{k+1} = \sum n_i[Y_i]$ over the irreducible components $Y_i \subset Y$ of $\delta$-dimension $k + 1$ with $n_i > 0$ (proof lines 4456-4461).

Show that each restriction $s_i = s|_{Y_i}$ is nonzero, hence a regular section, and use the computation of the first Chern class cap on an integral subscheme to identify its contribution (proof lines 4462-4465).
Use the definition of the cap to rewrite $c_1(\mathcal{L}) \cap [Y]_{k+1}$ as $\sum n_i[Z(s_i)]_k$, and conclude with the preparation lemma (proof lines 4466-4470).
proof_roadmap: Decomposition into irreducible components of dimension $k + 1$ (proof lines 4456-4461).
Nonvanishing of the restrictions and the first Chern class computation on one component (proof lines 4462-4465).
Weighted sum and the regrouping lemma (proof lines 4466-4470).
difficulty_reason: The lemma identifies the cap with the first Chern class of an invertible sheaf with the cycle class of the zero scheme of a section, assuming the two dimension bounds and the generic injectivity of multiplication by the section (statement lines 4431-4453). The proof decomposes the cycle of $Y$ into its components of maximal dimension, observes that the restrictions of the section remain nonzero and hence regular, computes each contribution with the first Chern class formula for an integral subscheme, and reassembles the pieces with the preparation lemma. The reduction to components and the reassembly are the substance, so the claim is H2.
